checks.message: Verify MFA is enforced, not just optional
checks.context: Setting MFA to OPTIONAL means users can skip it entirely. For any pool handling real users, set it to ON (TOTP) or use adaptive authentication. AWS Config flags pools without MFA as NON_COMPLIANT.

Without threat protection, Cognito won't detect compromised credentials, block suspicious sign-ins, or flag account takeover attempts. Threat protection requires the Cognito Plus feature plan. Use --user-pool-tier PLUS (CLI) or set UserPoolAddOns.AdvancedSecurityMode=ENFORCED (API) to enable it. This is the single most impactful security setting in Cognito and is flagged by AWS Security Hub (Cognito.1).

checks.message: Set a strong password policy: minimum 12 chars, require uppercase, lowercase, numbers, symbols
checks.context: Default Cognito password policy allows 8-char passwords with minimal complexity. Weak passwords are the #1 vector for account takeover in user pools exposed to the internet.

checks.message: Deletion protection not enabled on user pool
checks.context: Without deletion protection, a single delete-user-pool command permanently destroys all user accounts, credentials, and app clients. AWS Security Hub flags this as a finding (Cognito.6). Enable it on any pool used in production.

checks.message: Verify token expiry is not set too long
checks.context: Long-lived access tokens (default is 1 hour, refresh tokens default to 30 days) increase the window for token theft. Set access token validity to 15-60 minutes and refresh tokens to the minimum your app needs.

checks.message: Disable unused OAuth flows, especially implicit grant
checks.context: The implicit grant flow returns tokens in the URL fragment, which gets logged in browser history, server logs, and referrer headers. Only enable authorization_code flow for web apps.

checks.message: ALLOW_USER_PASSWORD_AUTH enabled - passwords sent in plaintext to Cognito API
checks.context: ALLOW_USER_PASSWORD_AUTH transmits the user's password directly to the Cognito API instead of using SRP (Secure Remote Password). If the request is intercepted or logged, passwords are exposed. Use ALLOW_USER_SRP_AUTH instead.

checks.message: User enumeration protection not enabled for --prevent-user-existence-errors
checks.context: Without ENABLED, Cognito returns different error messages for non-existent users vs wrong passwords, allowing attackers to enumerate valid usernames. Set to ENABLED to return generic errors for both cases.

checks.message: Token revocation disabled - stolen tokens cannot be invalidated after logout
checks.context: With token revocation disabled, refresh tokens cannot be revoked when a user signs out. A stolen refresh token remains valid until it naturally expires, allowing an attacker to maintain access even after the user logs out.

checks.message: Temporary passwords expire after 7 days by default
checks.context: If the user doesn't sign in within 7 days, the account goes into FORCE_CHANGE_PASSWORD state permanently. You'll need to resend the invitation. Consider setting a shorter expiry for security-sensitive pools.

checks.message: Setting a permanent password bypasses the forced-change flow
checks.context: Using --permanent skips the requirement for the user to set their own password on first login. Only use this for service accounts or automated testing and never for real user accounts.

checks.message: User pool deletion is permanent. All users, groups, and app clients are destroyed
checks.context: There is no export or recovery option. All user accounts, attributes, and credentials are gone. Any application using this pool's client IDs will break immediately.

checks.message: Verify you're not weakening MFA or password policy settings
checks.context: Pool updates can silently downgrade security settings. Changing MFA from ON to OPTIONAL or relaxing password complexity affects all existing and future users immediately.

Without --no-allow-unauthenticated-identities, the pool may grant AWS credentials to anonymous users. Only enable unauthenticated access if your app explicitly requires it (e.g. guest browsing with minimal permissions).

checks.message: Cognito identity pool allows unauthenticated identities
checks.context: Enabling unauthenticated identities grants temporary AWS credentials to anyone without authentication. The unauthenticated IAM role must be locked down to the absolute minimum permissions. Most apps don't need this at all.
